subject: Cross-border subprocessor flag: request for proofchain and scope confirmation

To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: security@dataproc.com
Date: 2029-05-16T08:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected subprocessor jurisdiction flagged during pen test

Hi Sofia,

During our recent pen test and supply-chain review we found that one of the telemetry processors called out in your listed vendor (EdgeFlow) appears to be routing some logs through a partner in Uruguay. Gamma Retail has data residency constraints for PII originating in the EU and our legal team flagged this as an unexpected jurisdiction.

Can you confirm:
- whether Redwood or EdgeFlow authorizes any subprocessor in Uruguay for telemetry or logging?
- a chain-of-custody / proofchain showing how logs transit (which hops, timestamps, and retention for each hop)?
- whether there is an onshore fallback/onsite routing option for EU-origin traffic?

This is urgent for our compliance scrum tomorrow; please treat as high priority.

Thanks,
Ana Delgado
Head of Security, Gamma Retail

Subject: Request: proofchain + manifest for telemetry processors (Gamma Retail escal.)

Hi Marco / EdgeFlow team —

Redwood customer Gamma Retail (contact: Ana Delgado) has flagged an apparent hop to a processor in Uruguay linked to EdgeFlow telemetry for our shared integration. Gamma requires provenance for EU-origin PII. Please provide the following by EOD 2029-05-17 (UTC):

1) A signed subprocessor manifest (PDF) listing all active subprocessors for telemetry/logging, including country of operation and purpose.
2) A machine-exportable chain-of-custody report (CSV preferred) showing recent transit hops for EU-origin traffic (at minimum: timestamp, source region, next-hop hostname/IP range, retention window at hop).
3) Confirmation whether the Uruguay hop is transient (eg, cache/edge) or persistent, and whether an EU-only routing/profile is available for customers who require residency.
4) Any associated SOC2 or ISO attestation references that cover the Uruguay partner.

This is an urgent compliance ask tied to a live deal (DEAL-8792). Please include any proofs or redaction-friendly artifacts as attachments. If there are escalation contacts for legal/security, include them in your reply.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts — Redwood Inference

Note: CC'ed Marissa in case procurement needs to coordinate an addendum.

From: Marco Ruiz <marco@edgeflow.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: edgeflow-support@edgeflow.io
Date: 2029-05-17T07:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: proofchain + manifest for telemetry processors (Gamma Retail escal.)

Kim / Sofia —

Thanks for the clear ask; apologies for the panic. We investigated and the short answer: EdgeFlow does route a small percentage of cache/ingest traffic through a regional partner in Uruguay for capacity smoothing during certain peak windows. That partner is a subcontractor (UruNet SA) and handles ephemeral buffering only — they are not a long-term storage or analytics provider.

Attached for your review:
- edgeflow_subprocessor_manifest_v2.pdf (signed, lists UruNet SA as a subcontractor, country, purpose)
- edgeflow_chain_of_custody_20290517.csv (recent 72h export with timestamps and hop hostnames; IP ranges redacted)

Quick answers inline:
- Is Uruguay transient? Yes — used as an ephemeral buffer during rolling upgrades and burst windows for LATAM/EU overflow; retention at UruNet is TTL=5 minutes for buffered payloads, nothing persisted to long-term storage.
- EU-only routing? Yes — we offer an EU-strict profile that pins traffic to our EU fabric. We can enable it for Gamma; it requires a config flag and a minor onboarding change (no additional charge).
- Attestations: UruNet currently falls under EdgeFlow's SOC2 scope; we included the attestation reference number in the manifest.

We redacted full IPs in the CSV but included hostnames + timestamps + retention TTL for each hop. If you need full IP ranges we can provide under an NDA/email-verified channel.

Let me know if this is sufficient or if you need an engineer-led call to walk through the CSV.

Regards,
Marco Ruiz
Head of Integrations — EdgeFlow

- They attached a signed manifest and a 72-hour chain-of-custody export. I've attached the filenames in our case record and uploaded to the shared drive for your review.
- EdgeFlow can flip on an EU-strict routing profile for Gamma if you want to eliminate the Uruguay hop entirely; this is a configuration change (no infra migration) and can be done within 48 hours after Gamma signs the small addendum.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Ana / Gamma: review the attached manifest + CSV in the shared drive link. If acceptable, reply "approve EU-routing addendum" and we'll coordinate the flip.
2) Kim/Legal: I recommend we run a one-paragraph addendum (scope: EU-routing profile; effective immediately for Gamma account) — Marissa will prep a draft and share a DocuSign link.
3) Ben/CS: schedule an engineer call with EdgeFlow and Gamma security for a short walkthrough of the CSV (if Gamma wants deeper network details).

If Gamma approves the addendum we can mitigate compliance risk in <72 hours. Thank you for the rapid escalation — appreciate everyone's quick coordination.

Best,
